must_read.title: Toward Sex-Specific Host Modulation Therapy for Periodontitis
must_read.abstract: Periodontitis, a leading cause of tooth loss worldwide, arises from a dysregulated host immune response, and males consistently show higher prevalence and more severe disease than females. This disparity historically has been attributed to behavioral/environmental factors, but growing evidence indicates that biological sex, acting through hormonal signaling and sex chromosome-linked genetic mechanisms, independently shapes periodontal immune responses and subsequent bone resorption. In this review, we examine preclinical and clinical evidence on the impact of biological sex on host modulation therapies to prevent periodontitis. The IL-1β/inflammasome pathway and osteoclast differentiation via receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)/osteoprotegerin (OPG) signaling both show clear sex-dependent regulation in experimental periodontitis, illustrating the biological complexity that single-target therapies must address in this heterogeneous condition. In a mouse model, inflammasome-mediated IL-1β signaling drives alveolar bone loss selectively in males, while females progress to comparable bone loss through IL-1β-independent mechanisms. IL-17 plays a dual role, driving inflammatory bone resorption while also supporting antimicrobial defense, and evidence points to this balance being sex dependent, with more severe effects observed in females when IL-17 signaling is disrupted. IL-6 is an established driver of periodontal bone loss, and although sex-specific data within periodontitis remain limited, sex-dependent anti-IL-6 receptor treatment responses have been observed in other inflammatory diseases that warrant further investigation. Complement-mediated immunity shows biological sex differences in humans and animal models, though whether these discrepancies directly influence periodontal disease progression needs to be determined. Resolvins and cyclooxygenase inhibitors also show sex-dependent effects outside the periodontal field. Collectively, this evidence positions biological sex as a tractable, currently underappreciated variable to improve host modulation strategies. Incorporating sex as a biological variable into preclinical and clinical periodontal research and ensuring sex-disaggregated data reporting offer a clear opportunity to develop precise, sex-informed nonsurgical therapeutics that better serve both male and female patients.

scan.title: Boosting Functional Dental Pulp Regeneration by a Biomimetic Self-assembling Hydrogel through Remodeling the Stem Cell Niche

scan.cluster: 生物材料表面/降解产物如…
scan.abstract: Cell-free strategies for dental pulp regeneration rely on the recruitment of endogenous stem cells, but cell entry alone is not sufficient. The stem cells require staged niche cues that support early mechanical adaptation and later coordinate odontogenic, angiogenic, and neural supportive responses. Here, we report RQK (RADA16/QP5/KLT), an injectable self-assembling peptide hydrogel designed to integrate extracellular matrix-like architecture with instructive bioactive cues for functional pulp regeneration. RQK combines the RADA16 (RAD) nanofibrous backbone with the amelogenin-derived odontogenic motif QP5 and the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mimetic angiogenic motif KLT. The hydrogel formed at 37°C, showed injectability and recovery, and could adapt to the irregular root canal space. In three-dimensional culture, RQK guided human dental pulp stem cells through a staged regenerative response. RQK first maintained stemness and mechanosensitive signaling, then promoted adhesion remodeling, odontogenic differentiation, enhanced angiogenic activity, and neural supportive effects. Transcriptomic analysis further linked this staged response to extracellular matrix interaction, cell adhesion, mechanosensitive signaling, and developmental programs. Molecular dynamics simulations and ultrastructural analyses suggested that interactions between RQK and collagen created a matrix environment favorable for odontogenic differentiation. Furthermore, evaluations across different stages in an infected immature beagle tooth model revealed that RQK promoted periapical healing and continued root development. Newly formed pulp-like tissue was more functional and showed odontoblast-like cell arrangement, vascular ingrowth, and neural tissue formation. These findings demonstrate that biomimetic niche reconstruction can guide endogenous stem cell behavior and improve cell-free dental pulp regeneration in vivo, providing a biomimetic framework for enhancing in situ tissue regeneration. Unlike conventional scaffold designs, RQK combines a nanofibrous matrix that mimics the extracellular matrix with odontogenic and angiogenic bioactive motifs. scan.title: Clinical outcomes of composite restorations with or without a glass ionomer liner after selective caries removal to soft dentin: a 36-month randomized controlled trial
scan.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Selective caries removal to soft dentin (SCR-SD) is currently recommended for the management of deep dentine caries lesions in permanent teeth. However, whether a pulp-protective liner is required after SCR-SD remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial compared the clinical performance and pulp vitality outcomes of composite resin restorations using a universal adhesive with or without a glass ionomer cement (GIC) liner after SCR-SD in deep caries lesions of permanent posterior teeth. METHODS: A randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted in 144 deep dentin caries lesions from 98 participants aged 9 to 55 years. After SCR-SD, lesions were randomly allocated to one of two restorative strategies: a universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode (SE) and composite resin without a GIC liner, or a conventional GIC liner followed by the same universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and composite resin (GIC + SE). Restorations were followed for 30-36 months. The primary outcome was restoration survival, assessed using selected FDI criteria. The secondary outcome was pulp vitality preservation. Survival analyses were performed using Weibull regression models. RESULTS: Of the 144 treated lesions, 117 were evaluated after 30-36 months. Restoration survival did not differ significantly between groups, with survival rates of 96.0% for SE and 92.4% for GIC + SE (p = 0.37). In contrast, pulp vitality preservation was significantly higher in the SE group than in the GIC + SE group, with success rates of 97.5% and 87.3%, respectively (p = 0.01). In the adjusted Weibull regression model, SE was associated with a lower risk of pulp vitality failure compared with GIC + SE. Restorative failure was also strongly associated with pulp vitality failure. CONCLUSIONS: The use of a GIC liner after SCR-SD did not improve restoration survival and was not associated with better pulp vitality preservation. Composite restorations using universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode placed directly over the remaining dentin showed favorable restorative and biological outcomes after 30-36 months. These findings suggest that routine liner placement after SCR-SD may not be necessary. scan.title: Opposing microbiome-mediated axes link modifiable lifestyles to health and chronic diseases
scan.domain: 口腔鳞癌的免疫微环境与微…
scan.cluster: 口腔鳞癌的免疫微环境与微…
scan.abstract: Analyses disentangling the role of the gut microbiome in linking lifestyle factors to health outcomes remain limited. Here, using fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort, we identified two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases. A health-associated axis enriched in microbial metabolism of dietary components was linked to plant-based, soy and dairy intake. In contrast, a disease-associated axis, enriched in oral-derived bacteria and pathobionts, was linked to refined carbohydrates and sedentary behavior. Starter culture microorganisms used to ferment foods did not show statistically significant mediation of the observed health effects. Alcohol was associated with both health- and disease-oriented mediation patterns involving microbial host-glycan utilization. Microbiome-defined health- and disease-oriented mediator axes were supported by fecal short-chain fatty acids and plasma cytokines from >1,700 individuals, revealing butyrate-associated anti-inflammatory and pro-inflammatory host profiles, respectively. Microbiome-based prediction (MADE) scores captured lifestyle-microbiome-disease mediation patterns and distinguished individual diseases across 13 independent external cohorts from the United States, China, Sweden, Russia and Australia. We identify the gut microbiome as a key mediator linking lifestyle to health and disease, providing a framework for microbiome-based assessment to guide lifestyle interventions for health promotion and disease prevention.
